In the answer it becomes clear that the Erinyes restrict their vengeance to the murder of blood relatives (even more clearly at V. 605); thus for them the murder of a husband is also not a ⟦3⟧, i.e. ⟦4⟧ (⟦5⟧. 734), ⟦6⟧ (⟦7⟧. ⟦8⟧), or no ⟦9⟧ (336), i.e. committed with one's own hand on one's own blood (⟦10⟧ ⟦11⟧). This "on one's own blood" is habitually supplied with these words, since this is the worst case of killing with one's own hand; of course ⟦12⟧ (⟦13⟧ ⟦14⟧, where, however, the narrower concept shines through), ⟦15⟧ also retain the general meaning.

Apollo thus, as the representative of a higher morality, equates the bond of marriage in beautiful and dignified words with the bonds of blood, and one only wonders that later in the legal dispute at Athens this argument is not brought forward again; cf. below.
